guides.title: Sports Day Gift and Prize Ideas for Schools | Ferrouswheel Bangalore
guides.description: Sports Day prize and return gift ideas that kids actually keep: medal hangers, metal bookmarks and keychains with your school crest. Plus how far ahead to order.
guides.h1: Sports Day Gift Ideas Kids Actually Keep
guides.intro: Most Sports Day gifts end up in a drawer by the end of the week. Plastic trophies crack, certificates get folded into school bags, and medals get lost. If you want something the kids hang on their wall for years, metal is hard to beat. Here's what schools order from us, and how to plan it.

p: A medal hanger gives the medal somewhere to live. We cut the child's sport into the design, and the school crest or name if you like. Every time they win something new, it goes on the same hanger.
They work well as first-place prizes, or as a gift for the whole team that wins the house cup.

If you want something for every child, not just the winners, bookmarks are the easiest choice. They're small and light, they survive a school bag, and the school crest comes out sharp even at this size.
You can add the event name and year so they remember which Sports Day it was.
Keychains are popular with older students and for staff. We can cut a different design for each house or team, so every group has its own.

sections.h2: 4. Something for the teachers and volunteers
p: The PE teachers and parent volunteers usually get nothing. A desk nameplate or a small plaque with the school crest is a simple way to say thank you.

200 pieces take us about 4 weeks to make, and we can only take a few bulk orders each month. Sports Day season (October to November) fills up first, so message us 6 to 8 weeks before the event if you can.
To get a quote, send us the quantity, your crest or logo in any format, and the date of the event. We'll send a design preview and a price. We can invoice against your purchase order.

guides.title: How to Display Medals: Ideas for Runners and Athletes | Ferrouswheel
guides.description: Medals in a shoebox? Simple ways to display them at home, how to choose a medal hanger, and how many medals one can hold. From a Bangalore metal workshop.
guides.intro: If you run, swim, cycle or play any sport seriously, medals pile up fast. Most people start with a shoebox and end up with a tangle of ribbons. Here are the common ways to put them on display, and what to think about before you pick one.

p: Hooks or a curtain rod: cheap and quick, but medals bunch up and it looks temporary.
A shadow box frame: neat for a few special medals, but you have to open it every time you add one, and it fills up quickly.

A medal hanger: a metal bar that goes on the wall, with the medals hanging from it. It's easy to add new medals, and it can be personalised with your name and sport. This is what most runners and athletes end up with.

sections.h2: How many medals will a hanger hold?
p: It depends on the length of the bar and how wide the ribbons are. Most ribbons are about 3 to 4 cm wide, so as a rough guide a 40 cm bar holds 10 to 12 medals side by side. You can hang two or three medals on the same spot as the collection grows.
If you race often, go longer than you think you need. Most people fill theirs faster than they expect.

The best medal hangers say something about the person. We cut your sport into the design: a runner, a swimmer, a cricketer, a badminton player. Then we add your name. You can also add a race name or a club logo.
For kids, a hanger with their name on it is a great way to encourage them. Every new medal goes up where they can see it.
Somewhere you see every day works best: a bedroom wall, a hallway, or above a desk. Use wall plugs rated for the weight, because a full set of medals is heavier than it looks.

sections.h2: A good gift for a runner
p: If someone you know just finished their first half marathon, a medal hanger with their name on it is a gift they'll actually use. Send us their name, their sport and any race you want on it.

guides.title: Personalised Metal Nameplate Ideas for Your Home | Ferrouswheel
guides.description: Nameplate ideas for front doors, kids' rooms and desks, which metal to choose for indoors and outdoors, and what to ask when ordering one as a housewarming gift.
guides.intro: A nameplate is the first thing people see at your door, and most of them look the same: a family name on a rectangle. A custom metal nameplate can say a lot more about who lives there. Here are some ideas, and a few practical things to get right.

p: Family name plus a shared hobby: a tennis racquet, a guitar, a car, or the family dog.
Kids' room signs: their name with the thing they're obsessed with right now, like football, dinosaurs or space.
Home office or desk plates: your name with something from your work or hobby, so the desk feels like yours.
Stainless steel is the safe choice for outside the front door. It handles Bangalore's rain without rusting.
Brass has a warm gold look that deepens over time. Copper starts bright and slowly darkens, which some people love.
Mild steel looks great indoors and costs less, but it isn't meant for outdoor use unless it's coated.
Not sure? Tell us where it's going and we'll suggest one.
Measure the space before you order. Next to a front door, something about the width of an A4 sheet reads well from the gate. Inside, for a kid's room door or a desk, smaller is better.
Send us a photo of the spot and we'll suggest a size.

A nameplate is one of the few housewarming gifts that gets used every day. To order one as a gift, you'll need the exact family name and spelling, and an idea of what they're into. If you're not sure, a clean design with just the name is a safe choice.
